source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect detailed data regarding the times, dates, and locations of all monitoring activities. This should include all measured parameters, such as particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulfur dioxide (SO2), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and specific hazardous air pollutants (HAPs) relevant to your industry. Ensure that the monitoring equipment is calibrated according to the manufacturer's instructions and that all calibration records are up-to-date.

3. Review the regulatory standards.
Understand the applicable local, regional, and national regulations for industrial emissions. Compare your monitoring data against these standards to identify any instances where emissions exceed the established limits.

4. Perform emission calculations.
Use your industry-specific emission factors and process data to calculate the actual emissions. Compare these calculated emissions with permitted levels. Make detailed notes of the methods used in calculations, the equations applied, and data sources.

5. Document
